label: input f during the original phase (weaker: j/n/p, <DEL>)
explanation: Fires mostly in the original phase (88% of mass) and at the delimiter (10%); almost never in the copy phase and never at t=0. The input token f dominates: f steps fire 13x the base rate and hold 52% of mass, including all of the top activations. Inputs j, n, p (about 4x each, ~10% of mass each) and <DEL> (1.5x) are weaker secondary triggers. Firing depends heavily on context: only about 25% of original-phase f steps fire. The rate is higher at early positions (t=1-4) and when the sequence starts with d, v, i or l (first_tok d is 4.5x). The strongest activations come on f after a d-initial prefix, e.g. d i d x w b b a f. Sequences full of e/o/x/s tend not to fire. Adding first-token or prefix conditions raised precision (to 0.5) but cut recall, so F1 never got above about 0.35. The context dependence looks distributed across the hidden state and is not captured by a simple predicate.
